name: Critical Incident Technique (CIT) Audit
phase: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [event X] triggers operational failure in [workflow Y]. We will verify this by collecting 15 detailed critical incident reports from practitioners, and consider it validated if ≥ 80% report that the incident caused acute workflow delays, compliance exposure, or direct financial loss.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Set explicit inclusion criteria for a critical incident: downtime, SLA breach or emergency briefing.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Ask practitioners to recount the most recent failure, the conditions before it, and what failed in response.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Build a chronological event map per incident: root trigger, compounding effects, downstream cost.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Establish explicit inclusion criteria for what constitutes a critical incident (e.g., unscheduled downtime, SLA breach, or emergency executive briefing).

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Interview qualified practitioners using the CIT protocol: "Recount the most recent operational failure in your workflow. What specific conditions preceded it? What interventions were deployed, and what systems failed?"

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Reconstruct a chronological event map for each incident, detailing the root triggers, secondary compounding effects, and downstream financial costs.

warning.label: Salience and Availability Bias
warning.text: Vivid crises are remembered clearly and mistaken for routine, recurring market needs.

warningFull: Participants recall dramatic, emotionally charged anomalies with extreme clarity, leading researchers to mistake infrequent operational crises for routine, recurring market needs.
